latin.209:
§. III.
Tertium, hujus, i. e. Reformationis Seculi, Molimen, FRANCOFURTANUM est, post fata Lutheri, Melanchthone tamen adhuc superstite, annis 1557. & 1558., ab ipsis Imperii Statibus & horum Antefignano, Ottone Henrico Palatino, susceptum, evocatis Francofurtum, 25. Theologis, hosque inter Joh. Pistorio, Andrea Hypperio, & Nicolao Rhodingo, Professoribus Marpurgensibus, rigidis vulgò habitis Calvinistis.
latin.210: ANNO PRIORI, Papistis, cum quibus erat colloquendum, dicunt Theologi congregati: Non esse inter se, qui erroneas foveant Opiniones, à Confessione alienas, Consensumque esse in fundamento.
latin.211: POSTERIORI ANNO, collatis rationibus, in hanc de Sacra Coena quoque Formulam (cujus summarium Autor quoque noster pagina 335. recitat) consentiunt: De hoc Articulo, inquiunt, in Ecclesiis nostris doceri debet juxta Augustanam Confessionem, nempe quod in hac Domini nostri Jesu Christi Ordinatione Sacrae Coenae, vere, vivificè & Substantialiter Christus praesens sit, & cum pane & vino sic ab ipso ordinatis, Corpus & Sanguinem suum manducandum & bibendum nobis Christianis exhibeat, atque testetur, quod ipsius membra simus, & quòd se ipsum una cum promissione Gratiae nobis donet, & quod in nobis sit efficax & operetur, quemadmodum Hilarius inquit: Haec sumta & hausta, faciunt, ut Christus sit in nobis & nos in ipso.
latin.212: Verba clarè loquuntur de actione seu usu: sicut & Paulus expressè de usu seu Actione inquit: Panis quem frangimus, est Communio Corporis Christi. Id enim de Pane extra usum intelligi non potest, sed hôc modo accipiendum est; hic Panis est res illa, quâ nobis Communio Corporis Christi exhibetur, & sic loquuntur veteres scriptores & Patres praecipui in Ecclesia.
latin.213: Irenaeus inquit: Eucharistia constat duabus rebus, Terrena & Coelesti, & Epiphanius ac Theodoretus clarè dicunt, quod natura & substantia maneat, & quod tamen cum Pane dona nobis dentur, videlicet Corpus & sanguis Christi. Postea nova locutiones introductae sunt: Panem mutari, sicut Baculus Mosis mutabatur in Serpentem. Crocius Comment. in August. Confess. pag. 204.

pass_a.209: §. III. The Third Effort of this, that is of the Reformation Century, is the FRANKFURT one, after the death of Luther, Melanchthon nevertheless still surviving, in the years 1557 and 1558, undertaken by the Imperial Estates themselves and their standard-bearer, Otto Henry the Palatine, twenty-five Theologians having been summoned to Frankfurt, and among these Johann Pistorius, Andreas Hyperius, and Nicolaus Rhodingus, Marburg Professors, commonly held to be rigid Calvinists.
pass_a.210: IN THE PRIOR YEAR, to the Papists with whom there was to be colloquy, the assembled Theologians say: that there is not among them anyone who fosters erroneous Opinions alien to the Confession, and that there is Consensus in the foundation.
pass_a.211: IN THE LATER YEAR, reasons having been compared, they also consent to this Formula concerning the Sacred Supper (whose summary our Author also recites at page 335): Concerning this Article, they say, it ought to be taught in our Churches according to the Augsburg Confession, namely that in this Ordinance of the Sacred Supper of our Lord Jesus Christ, Christ is truly, vivifically, and Substantially present, and with the bread and wine thus ordained by him exhibits his Body and Blood to be eaten and drunk to us Christians, and testifies that we are his members, and that he gives himself together with the promise of Grace to us, and that he is efficacious in us and works, just as Hilary says: These things taken and drunk make Christ to be in us and us in him.
pass_a.212: The words clearly speak of action or use: just as Paul also expressly says concerning use or Action: The bread which we break is the Communion of the Body of Christ. For that cannot be understood of Bread outside the use, but must be taken in this way; this Bread is that thing by which the Communion of the Body of Christ is exhibited to us, and thus speak the ancient writers and principal Fathers in the Church.
pass_a.213: Irenaeus says: the Eucharist consists of two things, Earthly and Heavenly, and Epiphanius and Theodoret clearly say that the nature and substance remain, and that nevertheless with the Bread gifts are given to us, namely the Body and blood of Christ. Afterwards new manners of speaking were introduced: that the Bread is changed, just as the Staff of Moses was changed into a Serpent. Crocius, Commentary on the Augsburg Confession, p. 204.

209: §. III. The third Consociation attempt of this Reformation century is the Frankfurt one.
It came after Luther’s death, while Melanchthon was still alive — in 1557 and 1558 — undertaken by the Imperial Estates and their leader, Otto Henry the Palatine.
Twenty-five theologians were called to Frankfurt; among them Johann Pistorius, Andreas Hyperius, and Nicolaus Rhodingus, Marburg professors commonly counted as rigid Calvinists.
210: In the prior year, the assembled theologians tell the Papists with whom they were to confer: none among them fosters erroneous opinions alien to the Confession, and they stand in consensus on the foundation.
211: In the later year, after comparing reasons, they also agree on a Formula for the Sacred Supper (our author summarizes it at p. 335).
On this article, they say, our churches must teach according to the Augsburg Confession: in the Lord’s ordinance of the Sacred Supper, Christ is truly, vivifically, and substantially present.

With the bread and wine he has so ordained, he exhibits his body and blood for Christians to eat and drink, testifies that we are his members, gives himself with the promise of grace, and works efficaciously in us — as Hilary says: what is taken and drunk makes Christ to be in us and us in him.
212: The words clearly speak of action or use — as Paul says expressly of use or action: the bread we break is the communion of the body of Christ.

That cannot mean bread outside the use; take it this way: this bread is the thing by which communion of Christ’s body is exhibited to us — and so speak the older writers and chief Fathers in the Church.
213: Irenaeus says the Eucharist consists of two things, earthly and heavenly; Epiphanius and Theodoret clearly say the nature and substance remain, yet with the bread gifts are given — namely Christ’s body and blood.
Later new phrases came in: that the bread is changed, as Moses’ staff was changed into a serpent (Crocius on the Augsburg Confession, p. 204).
